# Appeal of Denial — Lower Back (Lumbar) Fusion (CPT 22612)

**Governing Policy:** 2025 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – HMSA Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines (effective July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026)
https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2025-07/2025%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines%20-%20HMSA%20FINAL%20eff%20070125.pdf

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-05
**Member:** Quinn Foster
**Member ID:** W310107367
**Reference Number:** POC-D89C6A76F0-15779
**Plan:** HMSA (Hawaii Medical Service Association), Commercial/ACA, State of Hawaii
**Procedure:** Lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT 22612

---

Dear HMSA Member Advocacy & Appeals,

I am appealing the denial of my requested lumbar fusion surgery (CPT 22612). My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking HMSA to reconsider its decision.

## Why I am appealing

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I have reviewed the criteria cited in connection with my denial, and I want to bring something important to HMSA's attention: the criteria section I was given, and that appears to have been applied to my case, is written for **cervical** spine surgery, not for the **lumbar** fusion (CPT 22612) that was actually requested.

For example, the criteria at issue include:

> "Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Criteria Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF) – Multiple Levels When one of the two following criteria are met (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8):"

and

> "● Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy due to ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;"

These sections address the neck and cervical spine (upper extremity weakness, cervical radiculopathy, cervical myelopathy), not the lower back. My surgery is a lumbar fusion, addressing findings at L4-L5. I am not able to find, in the materials provided to me, any lumbar-fusion-specific criteria that were applied to my request, so I cannot confirm that the correct medical necessity standard was used to evaluate my case.

## The medical record supporting my surgery

Separately from the policy-language question above, I want to lay out the clinical findings in my chart, in my own words, so that a reviewer applying the correct (lumbar) criteria has the full picture:

- I have had 12 months of progressive lower back pain that is not relieved by rest.
- I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 visits, 2026-05-14 through 2026-07-09), including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for 8 months without adequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-11 gave only about 2 weeks of partial relief.
- An MRI of my lumbar spine on 2026-05-28 showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain radiating into my right calf.
- On examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on imaging.
- I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I do not smoke.

These are the facts in my medical record. I am asking HMSA to review my request against the medical necessity criteria that actually apply to lumbar fusion (CPT 22612), and to confirm whether the imaging and clinical findings above meet that standard.

## What I am asking for

1. Please reconsider the denial of CPT 22612 for my lumbar fusion.
2. Please confirm which specific medical necessity criteria — lumbar, not cervical — were applied to my request, and how my imaging and clinical findings were evaluated against them.
3. Please let me know if any additional records from Dr. Okafor would help complete this review.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-01** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I am submitting this appeal in writing as required. I understand I also have the right to request an external (IRO) review within 130 days if needed, though I understand my denial letter is the authoritative source for that deadline.

I am sending this appeal by mail to:

HMSA Member Advocacy & Appeals
Appeals Coordinator
P.O. Box 1958
Honolulu, HI 96805-1958

and/or by fax to 808-952-7546 or 808-948-8206 (Oahu).

Thank you for reconsidering my request. Please contact me if you need anything further.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Quinn Foster
Member ID: W310107367
[Phone number]
[Mailing address]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
